author: blu
body: The hash rides in the reply as well as the request, so a reply stands on its own rather than depending on the asker remembering what it asked. It costs 64 bytes and it means a reply can be checked by anyone holding it.

author: blu
body: Locate rides the same three-field shape as the work pair, and deliberately so: the bodies are wire-identical, so a reader that can take a work reply can take a locate reply by changing nothing but the tag it dispatches on. What differs is only what the third field means, and that difference is the whole point -- `payload` is content and is checked, `peers` is a hint and is used.
